Investigation confirms the mechanism. With `cacheComponents: true`, a default Link only does a **PPR (partial)** prefetch — the static shell — so `/catalog?category=X` still streams its dynamic heading/products and shows the loading state on click. Setting `prefetch={true}` on a Link maps to `FetchStrategy.Full`, which prefetches the **complete** RSC payload (the URL-specific heading + products) for each exact `/catalog?category=...` URL before the click.

part.text:
Done. Build passes; `/catalog` is correctly marked as Partial Prerender (PPR).

Change: added `prefetch={true}` to each category `<Link>` in `app/page.tsx`.

Why it works:
- URLs stay `/catalog?category=...`.
- With `cacheComponents: true`, a default Link does only a **PPR (partial)** prefetch — just the static shell — so the dynamic heading/products still stream on click (the "Loading category..." flash).
- `prefetch={true}` selects `FetchStrategy.Full`, which eagerly fetches the **complete** RSC payload (the URL-specific heading + products) for each exact `/catalog?category=...` URL while the link is visible.
- On click, Next navigates from the fully-warmed router cache: instant render, no loading state, and the click never waits on a server render.

The `<Suspense>` fallback in `app/catalog/page.tsx` stays as the safety net for cold/un-prefetched visits.
